29.5: In addition, you must sacrifice a male goat as a sin offering to purify yourselves and make yourselves right with the Lord.
29.6: These special sacrifices are in addition to your regular monthly and daily burnt offerings, and they must be given with their prescribed grain offerings and liquid offerings. These offerings are given as a special gift to the Lord, a pleasing aroma to him.
29.7: “Ten days later, on the tenth day of the same month, you must call another holy assembly. On that day, the Day of Atonement, the people must go without food and must do no ordinary work.
29.8: You must present a burnt offering as a pleasing aroma to the Lord. It will consist of one young bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all with no defects.
29.9: These offerings must be accompanied by the prescribed grain offerings of choice flour moistened with olive oil—six quarts of choice flour with the bull, four quarts of choice flour with the ram,
29.10: and two quarts of choice flour with each of the seven lambs.
29.11: You must also sacrifice one male goat for a sin offering. This is in addition to the sin offering of atonement and the regular daily burnt offering with its grain offering, and their accompanying liquid offerings.
29.12: “Five days later, on the fifteenth day of the same month, you must call another holy assembly of all the people, and you may do no ordinary work on that day. It is the beginning of the Festival of Shelters, a seven-day festival to the Lord.
29.13: On the first day of the festival, you must present a burnt offering as a special gift, a pleasing aroma to the Lord. It will consist of thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with no defects.
29.14: Each of these offerings must be accompanied by a grain offering of choice flour moistened with olive oil—six quarts for each of the thirteen bulls, four quarts for each of the two rams,
29.15: and two quarts for each of the fourteen lambs.
29.16: You must also sacrifice a male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its accompanying grain offering and liquid offering.
29.17: “On the second day of this seven-day festival, sacrifice twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with no defects.
29.18: Each of these offerings of bulls, rams, and lambs must be accompanied by its prescribed grain offering and liquid offering.
29.19: You must also sacrifice a male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its accompanying grain offering and liquid offering.
29.20: “On the third day of the festival, sacrifice eleven young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with no defects.
29.21: Each of these offerings of bulls, rams, and lambs must be accompanied by its prescribed grain offering and liquid offering.
29.22: You must also sacrifice a male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its accompanying grain offering and liquid offering.
29.23: “On the fourth day of the festival, sacrifice ten young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with no defects.
29.24: Each of these offerings of bulls, rams, and lambs must be accompanied by its prescribed grain offering and liquid offering.
29.25: You must also sacrifice a male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its accompanying grain offering and liquid offering.
29.26: “On the fifth day of the festival, sacrifice nine young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with no defects.
29.27: Each of these offerings of bulls, rams, and lambs must be accompanied by its prescribed grain offering and liquid offering.
29.28: You must also sacrifice a male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its accompanying grain offering and liquid offering.
29.29: “On the sixth day of the festival, sacrifice eight young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with no defects.
29.30: Each of these offerings of bulls, rams, and lambs must be accompanied by its prescribed grain offering and liquid offering.
29.31: You must also sacrifice a male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its accompanying grain offering and liquid offering.
29.32: “On the seventh day of the festival, sacrifice seven young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one-year-old male lambs, all with no defects.
29.33: Each of these offerings of bulls, rams, and lambs must be accompanied by its prescribed grain offering and liquid offering.
29.34: You must also sacrifice one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its accompanying grain offering and liquid offering.
29.35: “On the eighth day of the festival, proclaim another holy day. You must do no ordinary work on that day.
29.36: You must present a burnt offering as a special gift, a pleasing aroma to the Lord. It will consist of one young bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all with no defects.
29.37: Each of these offerings must be accompanied by its prescribed grain offering and liquid offering.
29.38: You must also sacrifice one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its accompanying grain offering and liquid offering.
29.39: “You must present these offerings to the Lord at your annual festivals. These are in addition to the sacrifices and offerings you present in connection with vows, or as voluntary offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings, liquid offerings, or peace offerings.”
29.40: So Moses gave all of these instructions to the people of Israel as the Lord had commanded him.

3.1: This is the family line of Aaron and Moses as it was recorded when the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai:
3.2: The names of Aaron’s sons were Nadab (the oldest), Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
3.3: These sons of Aaron were anointed and ordained to minister as priests.
3.4: But Nadab and Abihu died in the Lord’s presence in the wilderness of Sinai when they burned before the Lord the wrong kind of fire, different than he had commanded. Since they had no sons, this left only Eleazar and Ithamar to serve as priests with their father, Aaron.
3.5: Then the Lord said to Moses,
3.6: “Call forward the tribe of Levi, and present them to Aaron the priest to serve as his assistants.
3.7: They will serve Aaron and the whole community, performing their sacred duties in and around the Tabernacle.
3.8: They will also maintain all the furnishings of the sacred tent, serving in the Tabernacle on behalf of all the Israelites.
3.9: Assign the Levites to Aaron and his sons. They have been given from among all the people of Israel to serve as their assistants.
3.10: Appoint Aaron and his sons to carry out the duties of the priesthood. But any unauthorized person who goes too near the sanctuary must be put to death.”
3.11: And the Lord said to Moses,
3.12: “Look, I have chosen the Levites from among the Israelites to serve as substitutes for all the firstborn sons of the people of Israel. The Levites belong to me,
3.13: for all the firstborn males are mine. On the day I struck down all the firstborn sons of the Egyptians, I set apart for myself all the firstborn in Israel, both of people and of animals. They are mine; I am the Lord.”
3.14: The Lord spoke again to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai. He said,
3.15: “Record the names of the members of the tribe of Levi by their families and clans. List every male who is one month old or older.”
3.16: So Moses listed them, just as the Lord had commanded.
3.17: Levi had three sons, whose names were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
3.18: The clans descended from Gershon were named after two of his descendants, Libni and Shimei.
3.19: The clans descended from Kohath were named after four of his descendants, Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
3.20: The clans descended from Merari were named after two of his descendants, Mahli and Mushi. These were the Levite clans, listed according to their family groups.
3.21: The descendants of Gershon were composed of the clans descended from Libni and Shimei.
3.22: There were 7,500 males one month old or older among these Gershonite clans.
3.23: They were assigned the area to the west of the Tabernacle for their camp.
3.24: The leader of the Gershonite clans was Eliasaph son of Lael.
3.25: These two clans were responsible to care for the Tabernacle, including the sacred tent with its layers of coverings, the curtain at its entrance,
3.26: the curtains of the courtyard that surrounded the Tabernacle and altar, the curtain at the courtyard entrance, the ropes, and all the equipment related to their use.
3.27: The descendants of Kohath were composed of the clans descended from Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
3.28: There were 8,600 males one month old or older among these Kohathite clans. They were responsible for the care of the sanctuary,
3.29: and they were assigned the area south of the Tabernacle for their camp.
3.30: The leader of the Kohathite clans was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
3.31: These four clans were responsible for the care of the Ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the various articles used in the sanctuary, the inner curtain, and all the equipment related to their use.
3.32: Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, was the chief administrator over all the Levites, with special responsibility for the oversight of the sanctuary.
3.33: The descendants of Merari were composed of the clans descended from Mahli and Mushi.
3.34: There were 6,200 males one month old or older among these Merarite clans.
3.35: They were assigned the area north of the Tabernacle for their camp. The leader of the Merarite clans was Zuriel son of Abihail.
3.36: These two clans were responsible for the care of the frames supporting the Tabernacle, the crossbars, the pillars, the bases, and all the equipment related to their use.
3.37: They were also responsible for the posts of the courtyard and all their bases, pegs, and ropes.
3.38: The area in front of the Tabernacle, in the east toward the sunrise, was reserved for the tents of Moses and of Aaron and his sons, who had the final responsibility for the sanctuary on behalf of the people of Israel. Anyone other than a priest or Levite who went too near the sanctuary was to be put to death.
3.39: When Moses and Aaron counted the Levite clans at the Lord’s command, the total number was 22,000 males one month old or older.
3.40: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Now count all the firstborn sons in Israel who are one month old or older, and make a list of their names.
3.41: The Levites must be reserved for me as substitutes for the firstborn sons of Israel; I am the Lord. And the Levites’ livestock must be reserved for me as substitutes for the firstborn livestock of the whole nation of Israel.”
3.42: So Moses counted the firstborn sons of the people of Israel, just as the Lord had commanded.
3.43: The number of firstborn sons who were one month old or older was 22,273.
3.44: Then the Lord said to Moses,
3.45: “Take the Levites as substitutes for the firstborn sons of the people of Israel. And take the livestock of the Levites as substitutes for the firstborn livestock of the people of Israel. The Levites belong to me; I am the Lord.
3.46: There are 273 more firstborn sons of Israel than there are Levites. To redeem these extra firstborn sons,
3.47: collect five pieces of silver for each of them (each piece weighing the same as the sanctuary shekel, which equals twenty gerahs).
3.48: Give the silver to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for the extra firstborn sons.”
3.49: So Moses collected the silver for redeeming the firstborn sons of Israel who exceeded the number of Levites.
3.50: He collected 1,365 pieces of silver on behalf of these firstborn sons of Israel (each piece weighing the same as the sanctuary shekel).
3.51: And Moses gave the silver for the redemption to Aaron and his sons, just as the Lord had commanded.

13.1: The Lord now said to Moses,
13.2: “Send out men to explore the land of Canaan, the land I am giving to the Israelites. Send one leader from each of the twelve ancestral tribes.”
13.3: So Moses did as the Lord commanded him. He sent out twelve men, all tribal leaders of Israel, from their camp in the wilderness of Paran.
13.4: These were the tribes and the names of their leaders: Reuben: Shammua son of Zaccur
13.11: Manasseh son of Joseph: Gaddi son of Susi
13.16: These are the names of the men Moses sent out to explore the land. (Moses called Hoshea son of Nun by the name Joshua.)
13.17: Moses gave the men these instructions as he sent them out to explore the land: “Go north through the Negev into the hill country.
13.18: See what the land is like, and find out whether the people living there are strong or weak, few or many.
13.19: See what kind of land they live in. Is it good or bad? Do their towns have walls, or are they unprotected like open camps?
13.20: Is the soil fertile or poor? Are there many trees? Do your best to bring back samples of the crops you see.” (It happened to be the season for harvesting the first ripe grapes.)
13.21: So they went up and explored the land from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, near Lebo-hamath.
13.22: Going north, they passed through the Negev and arrived at Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai—all descendants of Anak—lived. (The ancient town of Hebron was founded seven years before the Egyptian city of Zoan.)
13.23: When they came to the valley of Eshcol, they cut down a branch with a single cluster of grapes so large that it took two of them to carry it on a pole between them! They also brought back samples of the pomegranates and figs.
13.24: That place was called the valley of Eshcol (which means “cluster”), because of the cluster of grapes the Israelite men cut there.
13.25: After exploring the land for forty days, the men returned
13.26: to Moses, Aaron, and the whole community of Israel at Kadesh in the wilderness of Paran. They reported to the whole community what they had seen and showed them the fruit they had taken from the land.
13.27: This was their report to Moses: “We entered the land you sent us to explore, and it is indeed a bountiful country—a land flowing with milk and honey. Here is the kind of fruit it produces.
13.28: But the people living there are powerful, and their towns are large and fortified. We even saw giants there, the descendants of Anak!
13.29: The Amalekites live in the Negev, and the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hill country. The Canaanites live along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea and along the Jordan Valley.”
13.30: But Caleb tried to quiet the people as they stood before Moses. “Let’s go at once to take the land,” he said. “We can certainly conquer it!”
13.31: But the other men who had explored the land with him disagreed. “We can’t go up against them! They are stronger than we are!”
13.32: So they spread this bad report about the land among the Israelites: “The land we traveled through and explored will devour anyone who goes to live there. All the people we saw were huge.
13.33: We even saw giants there, the descendants of Anak. Next to them we felt like grasshoppers, and that’s what they thought, too!”

25.1: While the Israelites were camped at Acacia Grove, some of the men defiled themselves by having sexual relations with local Moabite women.
25.2: These women invited them to attend sacrifices to their gods, so the Israelites feasted with them and worshiped the gods of Moab.
25.3: In this way, Israel joined in the worship of Baal of Peor, causing the Lord’s anger to blaze against his people.
25.4: The Lord issued the following command to Moses: “Seize all the ringleaders and execute them before the Lord in broad daylight, so his fierce anger will turn away from the people of Israel.”
25.5: So Moses ordered Israel’s judges, “Each of you must put to death the men under your authority who have joined in worshiping Baal of Peor.”
25.6: Just then one of the Israelite men brought a Midianite woman into his tent, right before the eyes of Moses and all the people, as everyone was weeping at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
25.7: When Phinehas son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron the priest saw this, he jumped up and left the assembly. He took a spear
25.8: and rushed after the man into his tent. Phinehas thrust the spear all the way through the man’s body and into the woman’s stomach. So the plague against the Israelites was stopped,
25.9: but not before 24,000 people had died.
25.10: Then the Lord said to Moses,
25.11: “Phinehas son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron the priest has turned my anger away from the Israelites by being as zealous among them as I was. So I stopped destroying all Israel as I had intended to do in my zealous anger.
25.12: Now tell him that I am making my special covenant of peace with him.
25.13: In this covenant, I give him and his descendants a permanent right to the priesthood, for in his zeal for me, his God, he purified the people of Israel, making them right with me.”
25.14: The Israelite man killed with the Midianite woman was named Zimri son of Salu, the leader of a family from the tribe of Simeon.
25.15: The woman’s name was Cozbi; she was the daughter of Zur, the leader of a Midianite clan.
25.16: Then the Lord said to Moses,
25.18: because they assaulted you with deceit and tricked you into worshiping Baal of Peor, and because of Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite leader, who was killed at the time of the plague because of what happened at Peor.”

33.1: This is the route the Israelites followed as they marched out of Egypt under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
33.2: At the Lord’s direction, Moses kept a written record of their progress. These are the stages of their march, identified by the different places where they stopped along the way.
33.3: They set out from the city of Rameses in early spring—on the fifteenth day of the first month—on the morning after the first Passover celebration. The people of Israel left defiantly, in full view of all the Egyptians.
33.4: Meanwhile, the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn sons, whom the Lord had killed the night before. The Lord had defeated the gods of Egypt that night with great acts of judgment!
33.5: After leaving Rameses, the Israelites set up camp at Succoth.
33.6: Then they left Succoth and camped at Etham on the edge of the wilderness.
33.7: They left Etham and turned back toward Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon, and camped near Migdol.
33.8: They left Pi-hahiroth and crossed the Red Sea into the wilderness beyond. Then they traveled for three days into the Etham wilderness and camped at Marah.
33.9: They left Marah and camped at Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees.
33.10: They left Elim and camped beside the Red Sea.
33.11: They left the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
33.12: They left the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
33.13: They left Dophkah and camped at Alush.
33.14: They left Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
33.15: They left Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
33.16: They left the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
33.17: They left Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
33.18: They left Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
33.19: They left Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
33.20: They left Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
33.21: They left Libnah and camped at Rissah.
33.22: They left Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
33.23: They left Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
33.24: They left Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
33.25: They left Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
33.26: They left Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
33.27: They left Tahath and camped at Terah.
33.28: They left Terah and camped at Mithcah.
33.29: They left Mithcah and camped at Hashmonah.
33.30: They left Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
33.31: They left Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
33.32: They left Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.
33.33: They left Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
33.34: They left Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
33.35: They left Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
33.36: They left Ezion-geber and camped at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.
33.37: They left Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, at the border of Edom.
33.38: While they were at the foot of Mount Hor, Aaron the priest was directed by the Lord to go up the mountain, and there he died. This happened in midsummer, on the first day of the fifth month of the fortieth year after Israel’s departure from Egypt.
33.39: Aaron was 123 years old when he died there on Mount Hor.
33.40: At that time the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard that the people of Israel were approaching his land.
33.41: Meanwhile, the Israelites left Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
33.42: Then they left Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
33.43: They left Punon and camped at Oboth.
33.44: They left Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim on the border of Moab.
33.45: They left Iye-abarim and camped at Dibon-gad.
33.46: They left Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
33.47: They left Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains east of the river, near Mount Nebo.
33.48: They left the mountains east of the river and camped on the plains of Moab beside the Jordan River, across from Jericho.
33.49: Along the Jordan River they camped from Beth-jeshimoth as far as the meadows of Acacia on the plains of Moab.
33.50: While they were camped near the Jordan River on the plains of Moab opposite Jericho, the Lord said to Moses,
33.51: “Give the following instructions to the people of Israel: When you cross the Jordan River into the land of Canaan,
33.52: you must drive out all the people living there. You must destroy all their carved and molten images and demolish all their pagan shrines.
33.53: Take possession of the land and settle in it, because I have given it to you to occupy.
33.54: You must distribute the land among the clans by sacred lot and in proportion to their size. A larger portion of land will be allotted to each of the larger clans, and a smaller portion will be allotted to each of the smaller clans. The decision of the sacred lot is final. In this way, the portions of land will be divided among your ancestral tribes.
33.55: But if you fail to drive out the people who live in the land, those who remain will be like splinters in your eyes and thorns in your sides. They will harass you in the land where you live.
33.56: And I will do to you what I had planned to do to them.”

32.1: The tribes of Reuben and Gad owned vast numbers of livestock. So when they saw that the lands of Jazer and Gilead were ideally suited for their flocks and herds,
32.2: they came to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the other leaders of the community. They said,
32.3: “Notice the towns of Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sibmah, Nebo, and Beon.
32.4: The Lord has conquered this whole area for the community of Israel, and it is ideally suited for all our livestock.
32.5: If we have found favor with you, please let us have this land as our property instead of giving us land across the Jordan River.”
32.6: “Do you intend to stay here while your brothers go across and do all the fighting?” Moses asked the men of Gad and Reuben.
32.7: “Why do you want to discourage the rest of the people of Israel from going across to the land the Lord has given them?
32.8: Your ancestors did the same thing when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to explore the land.
32.9: After they went up to the valley of Eshcol and explored the land, they discouraged the people of Israel from entering the land the Lord was giving them.
32.10: Then the Lord was very angry with them, and he vowed,
32.11: ‘Of all those I rescued from Egypt, no one who is twenty years old or older will ever see the land I swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, for they have not obeyed me wholeheartedly.
32.12: The only exceptions are Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, for they have wholeheartedly followed the Lord.’
32.13: “The Lord was angry with Israel and made them wander in the wilderness for forty years until the entire generation that sinned in the Lord’s sight had died.
32.14: But here you are, a brood of sinners, doing exactly the same thing! You are making the Lord even angrier with Israel.
32.15: If you turn away from him like this and he abandons them again in the wilderness, you will be responsible for destroying this entire nation!”
32.16: But they approached Moses and said, “We simply want to build pens for our livestock and fortified towns for our wives and children.
32.17: Then we will arm ourselves and lead our fellow Israelites into battle until we have brought them safely to their land. Meanwhile, our families will stay in the fortified towns we build here, so they will be safe from any attacks by the local people.
32.18: We will not return to our homes until all the people of Israel have received their portions of land.
32.19: But we do not claim any of the land on the other side of the Jordan. We would rather live here on the east side and accept this as our grant of land.”
32.20: Then Moses said, “If you keep your word and arm yourselves for the Lord’s battles,
32.21: and if your troops cross the Jordan and keep fighting until the Lord has driven out his enemies,
32.22: then you may return when the Lord has conquered the land. You will have fulfilled your duty to the Lord and to the rest of the people of Israel. And the land on the east side of the Jordan will be your property from the Lord.
32.23: But if you fail to keep your word, then you will have sinned against the Lord, and you may be sure that your sin will find you out.
32.24: Go ahead and build towns for your families and pens for your flocks, but do everything you have promised.”
32.25: Then the men of Gad and Reuben replied, “We, your servants, will follow your instructions exactly.
32.26: Our children, wives, flocks, and cattle will stay here in the towns of Gilead.
32.27: But all who are able to bear arms will cross over to fight for the Lord, just as you have said.”
32.28: So Moses gave orders to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the clans of Israel.
32.29: He said, “The men of Gad and Reuben who are armed for battle must cross the Jordan with you to fight for the Lord. If they do, give them the land of Gilead as their property when the land is conquered.
32.30: But if they refuse to arm themselves and cross over with you, then they must accept land with the rest of you in the land of Canaan.”
32.31: The tribes of Gad and Reuben said again, “We are your servants, and we will do as the Lord has commanded!
32.32: We will cross the Jordan into Canaan fully armed to fight for the Lord, but our property will be here on this side of the Jordan.”
32.33: So Moses assigned land to the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph. He gave them the territory of King Sihon of the Amorites and the land of King Og of Bashan—the whole land with its cities and surrounding lands.
32.34: The descendants of Gad built the towns of Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
32.36: Beth-nimrah, and Beth-haran. These were all fortified towns with pens for their flocks.
32.37: The descendants of Reuben built the towns of Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
32.38: Nebo, Baal-meon, and Sibmah. They changed the names of some of the towns they conquered and rebuilt.
32.39: Then the descendants of Makir of the tribe of Manasseh went to Gilead and conquered it, and they drove out the Amorites living there.
32.40: So Moses gave Gilead to the Makirites, descendants of Manasseh, and they settled there.
32.41: The people of Jair, another clan of the tribe of Manasseh, captured many of the towns in Gilead and changed the name of that region to the Towns of Jair.
32.42: Meanwhile, a man named Nobah captured the town of Kenath and its surrounding villages, and he renamed that area Nobah after himself.

24.1: By now Balaam realized that the Lord was determined to bless Israel, so he did not resort to divination as before. Instead, he turned and looked out toward the wilderness,
24.2: where he saw the people of Israel camped, tribe by tribe. Then the Spirit of God came upon him,
24.3: and this is the message he delivered: “This is the message of Balaam son of Beor, the message of the man whose eyes see clearly,
24.4: the message of one who hears the words of God, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who bows down with eyes wide open:
24.5: How beautiful are your tents, O Jacob; how lovely are your homes, O Israel!
24.6: They spread before me like palm groves, like gardens by the riverside. They are like tall trees planted by the Lord, like cedars beside the waters.
24.7: Water will flow from their buckets; their offspring have all they need. Their king will be greater than Agag; their kingdom will be exalted.
24.8: God brought them out of Egypt; for them he is as strong as a wild ox. He devours all the nations that oppose him, breaking their bones in pieces, shooting them with arrows.
24.9: Like a lion, Israel crouches and lies down; like a lioness, who dares to arouse her? Blessed is everyone who blesses you, O Israel, and cursed is everyone who curses you.”
24.10: King Balak flew into a rage against Balaam. He angrily clapped his hands and shouted, “I called you to curse my enemies! Instead, you have blessed them three times.
24.11: Now get out of here! Go back home! I promised to reward you richly, but the Lord has kept you from your reward.”
24.12: Balaam told Balak, “Don’t you remember what I told your messengers? I said,
24.13: ‘Even if Balak were to give me his palace filled with silver and gold, I would be powerless to do anything against the will of the Lord.’ I told you that I could say only what the Lord says!
24.14: Now I am returning to my own people. But first let me tell you what the Israelites will do to your people in the future.”
24.15: This is the message Balaam delivered: “This is the message of Balaam son of Beor, the message of the man whose eyes see clearly,
24.16: the message of one who hears the words of God, who has knowledge from the Most High, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who bows down with eyes wide open:
24.17: I see him, but not here and now. I perceive him, but far in the distant future. A star will rise from Jacob; a scepter will emerge from Israel. It will crush the heads of Moab’s people, cracking the skulls of the people of Sheth.
24.18: Edom will be taken over, and Seir, its enemy, will be conquered, while Israel marches on in triumph.
24.19: A ruler will rise in Jacob who will destroy the survivors of Ir.”
24.20: Then Balaam looked over toward the people of Amalek and delivered this message: “Amalek was the greatest of nations, but its destiny is destruction!”
24.21: Then he looked over toward the Kenites and delivered this message: “Your home is secure; your nest is set in the rocks.
24.22: But the Kenites will be destroyed when Assyria takes you captive.”
24.23: Balaam concluded his messages by saying: “Alas, who can survive unless God has willed it?
24.24: Ships will come from the coasts of Cyprus; they will oppress Assyria and afflict Eber, but they, too, will be utterly destroyed.”
24.25: Then Balaam left and returned home, and Balak also went on his way.

12.1: While they were at Hazeroth, Miriam and Aaron criticized Moses because he had married a Cushite woman.
12.2: They said, “Has the Lord spoken only through Moses? Hasn’t he spoken through us, too?” But the Lord heard them.
12.3: (Now Moses was very humble—more humble than any other person on earth.)
12.4: So immediately the Lord called to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam and said, “Go out to the Tabernacle, all three of you!” So the three of them went to the Tabernacle.
12.5: Then the Lord descended in the pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the Tabernacle. “Aaron and Miriam!” he called, and they stepped forward.
12.6: And the Lord said to them, “Now listen to what I say: “If there were prophets among you, I, the Lord, would reveal myself in visions. I would speak to them in dreams.
12.7: But not with my servant Moses. Of all my house, he is the one I trust.
12.8: I speak to him face to face, clearly, and not in riddles! He sees the Lord as he is. So why were you not afraid to criticize my servant Moses?”
12.9: The Lord was very angry with them, and he departed.
12.10: As the cloud moved from above the Tabernacle, there stood Miriam, her skin as white as snow from leprosy. When Aaron saw what had happened to her,
12.11: he cried out to Moses, “Oh, my master! Please don’t punish us for this sin we have so foolishly committed.
12.12: Don’t let her be like a stillborn baby, already decayed at birth.”
12.13: So Moses cried out to the Lord, “O God, I beg you, please heal her!”
12.14: But the Lord said to Moses, “If her father had done nothing more than spit in her face, wouldn’t she be defiled for seven days? So keep her outside the camp for seven days, and after that she may be accepted back.”
12.15: So Miriam was kept outside the camp for seven days, and the people waited until she was brought back before they traveled again.
12.16: Then they left Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.

2.1: Then the Lord gave these instructions to Moses and Aaron:
2.2: “When the Israelites set up camp, each tribe will be assigned its own area. The tribal divisions will camp beneath their family banners on all four sides of the Tabernacle, but at some distance from it.
2.3: “The divisions of Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun are to camp toward the sunrise on the east side of the Tabernacle, beneath their family banners. These are the names of the tribes, their leaders, and the numbers of their registered troops: Judah: Nahshon son of Amminadab: 74,600
2.9: So the total of all the troops on Judah’s side of the camp is 186,400. These three tribes are to lead the way whenever the Israelites travel to a new campsite.
2.10: “The divisions of Reuben, Simeon, and Gad are to camp on the south side of the Tabernacle, beneath their family banners. These are the names of the tribes, their leaders, and the numbers of their registered troops: Reuben: Elizur son of Shedeur: 46,500
2.16: So the total of all the troops on Reuben’s side of the camp is 151,450. These three tribes will be second in line whenever the Israelites travel.
2.17: “Then the Tabernacle, carried by the Levites, will set out from the middle of the camp. All the tribes are to travel in the same order that they camp, each in position under the appropriate family banner.
2.18: “The divisions of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Benjamin are to camp on the west side of the Tabernacle, beneath their family banners. These are the names of the tribes, their leaders, and the numbers of their registered troops: Ephraim: Elishama son of Ammihud: 40,500
2.24: So the total of all the troops on Ephraim’s side of the camp is 108,100. These three tribes will be third in line whenever the Israelites travel.
2.25: “The divisions of Dan, Asher, and Naphtali are to camp on the north side of the Tabernacle, beneath their family banners. These are the names of the tribes, their leaders, and the numbers of their registered troops: Dan: Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai: 62,700
2.31: So the total of all the troops on Dan’s side of the camp is 157,600. These three tribes will be last, marching under their banners whenever the Israelites travel.”
2.32: In summary, the troops of Israel listed by their families totaled 603,550.
2.33: But as the Lord had commanded, the Levites were not included in this registration.
2.34: So the people of Israel did everything as the Lord had commanded Moses. Each clan and family set up camp and marched under their banners exactly as the Lord had instructed them.

28.2: “Give these instructions to the people of Israel: The offerings you present as special gifts are a pleasing aroma to me; they are my food. See to it that they are brought at the appointed times and offered according to my instructions.
28.3: “Say to the people: This is the special gift you must present to the Lord as your daily burnt offering. You must offer two one-year-old male lambs with no defects.
28.4: Sacrifice one lamb in the morning and the other in the evening.
28.5: With each lamb you must offer a grain offering of two quarts of choice flour mixed with one quart of pure oil of pressed olives.
28.6: This is the regular burnt offering instituted at Mount Sinai as a special gift, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
28.7: Along with it you must present the proper liquid offering of one quart of alcoholic drink with each lamb, poured out in the Holy Place as an offering to the Lord.
28.8: Offer the second lamb in the evening with the same grain offering and liquid offering. It, too, is a special gift, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
28.9: “On the Sabbath day, sacrifice two one-year-old male lambs with no defects. They must be accompanied by a grain offering of four quarts of choice flour moistened with olive oil, and a liquid offering.
28.10: This is the burnt offering to be presented each Sabbath day, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its accompanying liquid offering.
28.11: “On the first day of each month, present an extra burnt offering to the Lord of two young bulls, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all with no defects.
28.12: These must be accompanied by grain offerings of choice flour moistened with olive oil—six quarts with each bull, four quarts with the ram,
28.13: and two quarts with each lamb. This burnt offering will be a special gift, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
28.14: You must also present a liquid offering with each sacrifice: two quarts of wine for each bull, a third of a gallon for the ram, and one quart for each lamb. Present this monthly burnt offering on the first day of each month throughout the year.
28.15: “On the first day of each month, you must also offer one male goat for a sin offering to the Lord. This is in addition to the regular burnt offering and its accompanying liquid offering.
28.16: “On the fourteenth day of the first month, you must celebrate the Lord’s Passover.
28.17: On the following day—the fifteenth day of the month—a joyous, seven-day festival will begin, but no bread made with yeast may be eaten.
28.18: The first day of the festival will be an official day for holy assembly, and no ordinary work may be done on that day.
28.19: As a special gift you must present a burnt offering to the Lord—two young bulls, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs, all with no defects.
28.20: These will be accompanied by grain offerings of choice flour moistened with olive oil—six quarts with each bull, four quarts with the ram,
28.21: and two quarts with each of the seven lambs.
28.22: You must also offer a male goat as a sin offering to purify yourselves and make yourselves right with the Lord.
28.23: Present these offerings in addition to your regular morning burnt offering.
28.24: On each of the seven days of the festival, this is how you must prepare the food offering that is presented as a special gift, a pleasing aroma to the Lord. These will be offered in addition to the regular burnt offerings and liquid offerings.
28.25: The seventh day of the festival will be another official day for holy assembly, and no ordinary work may be done on that day.
28.26: “At the Festival of Harvest, when you present the first of your new grain to the Lord, you must call an official day for holy assembly, and you may do no ordinary work on that day.
28.27: Present a special burnt offering on that day as a pleasing aroma to the Lord. It will consist of two young bulls, one ram, and seven one-year-old male lambs.
28.28: These will be accompanied by grain offerings of choice flour moistened with olive oil—six quarts with each bull, four quarts with the ram,
28.29: and two quarts with each of the seven lambs.
28.30: Also, offer one male goat to purify yourselves and make yourselves right with the Lord.
28.31: Prepare these special burnt offerings, along with their liquid offerings, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its accompanying grain offering. Be sure that all the animals you sacrifice have no defects.

11.1: Soon the people began to complain about their hardship, and the Lord heard everything they said. Then the Lord’s anger blazed against them, and he sent a fire to rage among them, and he destroyed some of the people in the outskirts of the camp.
11.2: Then the people screamed to Moses for help, and when he prayed to the Lord, the fire stopped.
11.3: After that, the area was known as Taberah (which means “the place of burning”), because fire from the Lord had burned among them there.
11.4: Then the foreign rabble who were traveling with the Israelites began to crave the good things of Egypt. And the people of Israel also began to complain. “Oh, for some meat!” they exclaimed.
11.5: “We remember the fish we used to eat for free in Egypt. And we had all the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic we wanted.
11.6: But now our appetites are gone. All we ever see is this manna!”
11.7: The manna looked like small coriander seeds, and it was pale yellow like gum resin.
11.8: The people would go out and gather it from the ground. They made flour by grinding it with hand mills or pounding it in mortars. Then they boiled it in a pot and made it into flat cakes. These cakes tasted like pastries baked with olive oil.
11.9: The manna came down on the camp with the dew during the night.
11.10: Moses heard all the families standing in the doorways of their tents whining, and the Lord became extremely angry. Moses was also very aggravated.
11.11: And Moses said to the Lord, “Why are you treating me, your servant, so harshly? Have mercy on me! What did I do to deserve the burden of all these people?
11.12: Did I give birth to them? Did I bring them into the world? Why did you tell me to carry them in my arms like a mother carries a nursing baby? How can I carry them to the land you swore to give their ancestors?
11.13: Where am I supposed to get meat for all these people? They keep whining to me, saying, ‘Give us meat to eat!’
11.14: I can’t carry all these people by myself! The load is far too heavy!
11.15: If this is how you intend to treat me, just go ahead and kill me. Do me a favor and spare me this misery!”
11.16: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Gather before me seventy men who are recognized as elders and leaders of Israel. Bring them to the Tabernacle to stand there with you.
11.17: I will come down and talk to you there. I will take some of the Spirit that is upon you, and I will put the Spirit upon them also. They will bear the burden of the people along with you, so you will not have to carry it alone.
11.18: “And say to the people, ‘Purify yourselves, for tomorrow you will have meat to eat. You were whining, and the Lord heard you when you cried, “Oh, for some meat! We were better off in Egypt!” Now the Lord will give you meat, and you will have to eat it.
11.19: And it won’t be for just a day or two, or for five or ten or even twenty.
11.20: You will eat it for a whole month until you gag and are sick of it. For you have rejected the Lord, who is here among you, and you have whined to him, saying, “Why did we ever leave Egypt?”’”
11.21: But Moses responded to the Lord, “There are 600,000 foot soldiers here with me, and yet you say, ‘I will give them meat for a whole month!’
11.22: Even if we butchered all our flocks and herds, would that satisfy them? Even if we caught all the fish in the sea, would that be enough?”
11.23: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Has my arm lost its power? Now you will see whether or not my word comes true!”
11.24: So Moses went out and reported the Lord’s words to the people. He gathered the seventy elders and stationed them around the Tabernacle.
11.25: And the Lord came down in the cloud and spoke to Moses. Then he gave the seventy elders the same Spirit that was upon Moses. And when the Spirit rested upon them, they prophesied. But this never happened again.
11.26: Two men, Eldad and Medad, had stayed behind in the camp. They were listed among the elders, but they had not gone out to the Tabernacle. Yet the Spirit rested upon them as well, so they prophesied there in the camp.
11.27: A young man ran and reported to Moses, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!”
11.28: Joshua son of Nun, who had been Moses’ assistant since his youth, protested, “Moses, my master, make them stop!”
11.29: But Moses replied, “Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all the Lord’s people were prophets and that the Lord would put his Spirit upon them all!”
11.30: Then Moses returned to the camp with the elders of Israel.
11.31: Now the Lord sent a wind that brought quail from the sea and let them fall all around the camp. For miles in every direction there were quail flying about three feet above the ground.
11.32: So the people went out and caught quail all that day and throughout the night and all the next day, too. No one gathered less than fifty bushels! They spread the quail all around the camp to dry.
11.33: But while they were gorging themselves on the meat—while it was still in their mouths—the anger of the Lord blazed against the people, and he struck them with a severe plague.
11.34: So that place was called Kibroth-hattaavah (which means “graves of gluttony”) because there they buried the people who had craved meat from Egypt.
11.35: From Kibroth-hattaavah the Israelites traveled to Hazeroth, where they stayed for some time.

1.1: A year after Israel’s departure from Egypt, the Lord spoke to Moses in the Tabernacle in the wilderness of Sinai. On the first day of the second month of that year he said,
1.2: “From the whole community of Israel, record the names of all the warriors by their clans and families. List all the men
1.3: twenty years old or older who are able to go to war. You and Aaron must register the troops,
1.4: and you will be assisted by one family leader from each tribe.
1.5: “These are the tribes and the names of the leaders who will assist you: Reuben: Elizur son of Shedeur
1.10: Ephraim son of Joseph: Elishama son of Ammihud; Manasseh son of Joseph: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur
1.16: These are the chosen leaders of the community, the leaders of their ancestral tribes, the heads of the clans of Israel.”
1.17: So Moses and Aaron called together these chosen leaders,
1.18: and they assembled the whole community of Israel on that very day. All the people were registered according to their ancestry by their clans and families. The men of Israel who were twenty years old or older were listed one by one,
1.19: just as the Lord had commanded Moses. So Moses recorded their names in the wilderness of Sinai.
1.20: This is the number of men twenty years old or older who were able to go to war, as their names were listed in the records of their clans and families: Reuben (Jacob’s oldest son): 46,500
1.44: These were the men registered by Moses and Aaron and the twelve leaders of Israel, all listed according to their ancestral descent.
1.45: They were registered by families—all the men of Israel who were twenty years old or older and able to go to war.
1.47: But this total did not include the Levites.
1.48: For the Lord had said to Moses,
1.49: “Do not include the tribe of Levi in the registration; do not count them with the rest of the Israelites.
1.50: Put the Levites in charge of the Tabernacle of the Covenant, along with all its furnishings and equipment. They must carry the Tabernacle and all its furnishings as you travel, and they must take care of it and camp around it.
1.51: Whenever it is time for the Tabernacle to move, the Levites will take it down. And when it is time to stop, they will set it up again. But any unauthorized person who goes too near the Tabernacle must be put to death.
1.52: Each tribe of Israel will camp in a designated area with its own family banner.
1.53: But the Levites will camp around the Tabernacle of the Covenant to protect the community of Israel from the Lord’s anger. The Levites are responsible to stand guard around the Tabernacle.”
1.54: So the Israelites did everything just as the Lord had commanded Moses.

31.1: Then the Lord said to Moses,
31.2: “On behalf of the people of Israel, take revenge on the Midianites for leading them into idolatry. After that, you will die and join your ancestors.”
31.3: So Moses said to the people, “Choose some men, and arm them to fight the Lord’s war of revenge against Midian.
31.4: From each tribe of Israel, send 1,000 men into battle.”
31.5: So they chose 1,000 men from each tribe of Israel, a total of 12,000 men armed for battle.
31.6: Then Moses sent them out, 1,000 men from each tribe, and Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest led them into battle. They carried along the holy objects of the sanctuary and the trumpets for sounding the charge.
31.7: They attacked Midian as the Lord had commanded Moses, and they killed all the men.
31.8: All five of the Midianite kings—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba—died in the battle. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
31.9: Then the Israelite army captured the Midianite women and children and seized their cattle and flocks and all their wealth as plunder.
31.10: They burned all the towns and villages where the Midianites had lived.
31.11: After they had gathered the plunder and captives, both people and animals,
31.12: they brought them all to Moses and Eleazar the priest, and to the whole community of Israel, which was camped on the plains of Moab beside the Jordan River, across from Jericho.
31.13: Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the community went to meet them outside the camp.
31.14: But Moses was furious with all the generals and captains who had returned from the battle.
31.15: “Why have you let all the women live?” he demanded.
31.16: “These are the very ones who followed Balaam’s advice and caused the people of Israel to rebel against the Lord at Mount Peor. They are the ones who caused the plague to strike the Lord’s people.
31.17: So kill all the boys and all the women who have had intercourse with a man.
31.18: Only the young girls who are virgins may live; you may keep them for yourselves.
31.19: And all of you who have killed anyone or touched a dead body must stay outside the camp for seven days. You must purify yourselves and your captives on the third and seventh days.
31.20: Purify all your clothing, too, and everything made of leather, goat hair, or wood.”
31.21: Then Eleazar the priest said to the men who were in the battle, “The Lord has given Moses this legal requirement:
31.22: Anything made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, or lead—
31.23: that is, all metals that do not burn—must be passed through fire in order to be made ceremonially pure. These metal objects must then be further purified with the water of purification. But everything that burns must be purified by the water alone.
31.24: On the seventh day you must wash your clothes and be purified. Then you may return to the camp.”
31.25: And the Lord said to Moses,
31.26: “You and Eleazar the priest and the family leaders of each tribe are to make a list of all the plunder taken in the battle, including the people and animals.
31.27: Then divide the plunder into two parts, and give half to the men who fought the battle and half to the rest of the people.
31.28: From the army’s portion, first give the Lord his share of the plunder—one of every 500 of the prisoners and of the cattle, donkeys, sheep, and goats.
31.29: Give this share of the army’s half to Eleazar the priest as an offering to the Lord.
31.30: From the half that belongs to the people of Israel, take one of every fifty of the prisoners and of the cattle, donkeys, sheep, goats, and other animals. Give this share to the Levites, who are in charge of maintaining the Lord’s Tabernacle.”
31.31: So Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the Lord commanded Moses.
31.32: The plunder remaining from everything the fighting men had taken totaled 675,000 sheep and goats,
31.36: Half of the plunder was given to the fighting men. It totaled 337,500 sheep and goats,
31.37: of which 675 were the Lord’s share
31.38: 36,000 cattle, of which 72 were the Lord’s share
31.39: 30,500 donkeys, of which 61 were the Lord’s share
31.40: and 16,000 virgin girls, of whom 32 were the Lord’s share.
31.41: Moses gave all the Lord’s share to Eleazar the priest, just as the Lord had directed him.
31.42: Half of the plunder belonged to the people of Israel, and Moses separated it from the half belonging to the fighting men.
31.47: From the half-share given to the people, Moses took one of every fifty prisoners and animals and gave them to the Levites, who maintained the Lord’s Tabernacle. All this was done as the Lord had commanded Moses.
31.48: Then all the generals and captains came to Moses
31.49: and said, “We, your servants, have accounted for all the men who went out to battle under our command; not one of us is missing!
31.50: So we are presenting the items of gold we captured as an offering to the Lord from our share of the plunder—armbands, bracelets, rings, earrings, and necklaces. This will purify our lives before the Lord and make us right with him.”
31.51: So Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from all the military commanders—all kinds of jewelry and crafted objects.
31.52: In all, the gold that the generals and captains presented as a gift to the Lord weighed about 420 pounds.
31.53: All the fighting men had taken some of the plunder for themselves.
31.54: So Moses and Eleazar the priest accepted the gifts from the generals and captains and brought the gold to the Tabernacle as a reminder to the Lord that the people of Israel belong to him.

27.1: One day a petition was presented by the daughters of Zelophehad—Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. Their father, Zelophehad, was a descendant of Hepher son of Gilead, son of Makir, son of Manasseh, son of Joseph.
27.2: These women stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the tribal leaders, and the entire community at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
27.3: “Our father died in the wilderness,” they said. “He was not among Korah’s followers, who rebelled against the Lord; he died because of his own sin. But he had no sons.
27.4: Why should the name of our father disappear from his clan just because he had no sons? Give us property along with the rest of our relatives.”
27.5: So Moses brought their case before the Lord.
27.6: And the Lord replied to Moses,
27.7: “The claim of the daughters of Zelophehad is legitimate. You must give them a grant of land along with their father’s relatives. Assign them the property that would have been given to their father.
27.8: “And give the following instructions to the people of Israel: If a man dies and has no son, then give his inheritance to his daughters.
27.9: And if he has no daughter either, transfer his inheritance to his brothers.
27.10: If he has no brothers, give his inheritance to his father’s brothers.
27.11: But if his father has no brothers, give his inheritance to the nearest relative in his clan. This is a legal requirement for the people of Israel, just as the Lord commanded Moses.”
27.12: One day the Lord said to Moses, “Climb one of the mountains east of the river, and look out over the land I have given the people of Israel.
27.13: After you have seen it, you will die like your brother, Aaron,
27.14: for you both rebelled against my instructions in the wilderness of Zin. When the people of Israel rebelled, you failed to demonstrate my holiness to them at the waters.” (These are the waters of Meribah at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.)
27.15: Then Moses said to the Lord,
27.16: “O Lord, you are the God who gives breath to all creatures. Please appoint a new man as leader for the community.
27.17: Give them someone who will guide them wherever they go and will lead them into battle, so the community of the Lord will not be like sheep without a shepherd.”
27.18: The Lord replied, “Take Joshua son of Nun, who has the Spirit in him, and lay your hands on him.
27.19: Present him to Eleazar the priest before the whole community, and publicly commission him to lead the people.
27.20: Transfer some of your authority to him so the whole community of Israel will obey him.
27.21: When direction from the Lord is needed, Joshua will stand before Eleazar the priest, who will use the Urim—one of the sacred lots cast before the Lord—to determine his will. This is how Joshua and the rest of the community of Israel will determine everything they should do.”
27.22: So Moses did as the Lord commanded. He presented Joshua to Eleazar the priest and the whole community.
27.23: Moses laid his hands on him and commissioned him to lead the people, just as the Lord had commanded through Moses.

26.1: After the plague had ended, the Lord said to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest,
26.2: “From the whole community of Israel, record the names of all the warriors by their families. List all the men twenty years old or older who are able to go to war.”
26.3: So there on the plains of Moab beside the Jordan River, across from Jericho, Moses and Eleazar the priest issued these instructions to the leaders of Israel:
26.4: “List all the men of Israel twenty years old and older, just as the Lord commanded Moses.” This is the record of all the descendants of Israel who came out of Egypt.
26.5: These were the clans descended from the sons of Reuben, Jacob’s oldest son: The Hanochite clan, named after their ancestor Hanoch. The Palluite clan, named after their ancestor Pallu.
26.6: The Hezronite clan, named after their ancestor Hezron. The Carmite clan, named after their ancestor Carmi.
26.7: These were the clans of Reuben. Their registered troops numbered 43,730.
26.8: Pallu was the ancestor of Eliab,
26.9: and Eliab was the father of Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. This Dathan and Abiram are the same community leaders who conspired with Korah against Moses and Aaron, rebelling against the Lord.
26.10: But the earth opened up its mouth and swallowed them with Korah, and fire devoured 250 of their followers. This served as a warning to the entire nation of Israel.
26.11: However, the sons of Korah did not die that day.
26.12: These were the clans descended from the sons of Simeon: The Jemuelite clan, named after their ancestor Jemuel. The Jaminite clan, named after their ancestor Jamin. The Jakinite clan, named after their ancestor Jakin.
26.13: The Zoharite clan, named after their ancestor Zohar. The Shaulite clan, named after their ancestor Shaul.
26.14: These were the clans of Simeon. Their registered troops numbered 22,200.
26.15: These were the clans descended from the sons of Gad: The Zephonite clan, named after their ancestor Zephon. The Haggite clan, named after their ancestor Haggi. The Shunite clan, named after their ancestor Shuni.
26.16: The Oznite clan, named after their ancestor Ozni. The Erite clan, named after their ancestor Eri.
26.17: The Arodite clan, named after their ancestor Arodi. The Arelite clan, named after their ancestor Areli.
26.18: These were the clans of Gad. Their registered troops numbered 40,500.
26.19: Judah had two sons, Er and Onan, who had died in the land of Canaan.
26.20: These were the clans descended from Judah’s surviving sons: The Shelanite clan, named after their ancestor Shelah. The Perezite clan, named after their ancestor Perez. The Zerahite clan, named after their ancestor Zerah.
26.21: These were the subclans descended from the Perezites: The Hezronites, named after their ancestor Hezron. The Hamulites, named after their ancestor Hamul.
26.22: These were the clans of Judah. Their registered troops numbered 76,500.
26.23: These were the clans descended from the sons of Issachar: The Tolaite clan, named after their ancestor Tola. The Puite clan, named after their ancestor Puah.
26.24: The Jashubite clan, named after their ancestor Jashub. The Shimronite clan, named after their ancestor Shimron.
26.25: These were the clans of Issachar. Their registered troops numbered 64,300.
26.26: These were the clans descended from the sons of Zebulun: The Seredite clan, named after their ancestor Sered. The Elonite clan, named after their ancestor Elon. The Jahleelite clan, named after their ancestor Jahleel.
26.27: These were the clans of Zebulun. Their registered troops numbered 60,500.
26.28: Two clans were descended from Joseph through Manasseh and Ephraim.
26.29: These were the clans descended from Manasseh: The Makirite clan, named after their ancestor Makir. The Gileadite clan, named after their ancestor Gilead, Makir’s son.
26.30: These were the subclans descended from the Gileadites: The Iezerites, named after their ancestor Iezer. The Helekites, named after their ancestor Helek.
26.31: The Asrielites, named after their ancestor Asriel. The Shechemites, named after their ancestor Shechem.
26.32: The Shemidaites, named after their ancestor Shemida. The Hepherites, named after their ancestor Hepher.
26.33: (One of Hepher’s descendants, Zelophehad, had no sons, but his daughters’ names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.)
26.34: These were the clans of Manasseh. Their registered troops numbered 52,700.
26.35: These were the clans descended from the sons of Ephraim: The Shuthelahite clan, named after their ancestor Shuthelah. The Bekerite clan, named after their ancestor Beker. The Tahanite clan, named after their ancestor Tahan.
26.36: This was the subclan descended from the Shuthelahites: The Eranites, named after their ancestor Eran.
26.37: These were the clans of Ephraim. Their registered troops numbered 32,500. These clans of Manasseh and Ephraim were all descendants of Joseph.
26.38: These were the clans descended from the sons of Benjamin: The Belaite clan, named after their ancestor Bela. The Ashbelite clan, named after their ancestor Ashbel. The Ahiramite clan, named after their ancestor Ahiram.
26.39: The Shuphamite clan, named after their ancestor Shupham. The Huphamite clan, named after their ancestor Hupham.
26.40: These were the subclans descended from the Belaites: The Ardites, named after their ancestor Ard. The Naamites, named after their ancestor Naaman.
26.41: These were the clans of Benjamin. Their registered troops numbered 45,600.
26.42: These were the clans descended from the sons of Dan: The Shuhamite clan, named after their ancestor Shuham.
26.43: These were the Shuhamite clans of Dan. Their registered troops numbered 64,400.
26.44: These were the clans descended from the sons of Asher: The Imnite clan, named after their ancestor Imnah. The Ishvite clan, named after their ancestor Ishvi. The Beriite clan, named after their ancestor Beriah.
26.45: These were the subclans descended from the Beriites: The Heberites, named after their ancestor Heber. The Malkielites, named after their ancestor Malkiel.
26.46: Asher also had a daughter named Serah.
26.47: These were the clans of Asher. Their registered troops numbered 53,400.
26.48: These were the clans descended from the sons of Naphtali: The Jahzeelite clan, named after their ancestor Jahzeel. The Gunite clan, named after their ancestor Guni.
26.49: The Jezerite clan, named after their ancestor Jezer. The Shillemite clan, named after their ancestor Shillem.
26.50: These were the clans of Naphtali. Their registered troops numbered 45,400.
26.51: In summary, the registered troops of all Israel numbered 601,730.
26.52: Then the Lord said to Moses,
26.53: “Divide the land among the tribes, and distribute the grants of land in proportion to the tribes’ populations, as indicated by the number of names on the list.
26.54: Give the larger tribes more land and the smaller tribes less land, each group receiving a grant in proportion to the size of its population.
26.55: But you must assign the land by lot, and give land to each ancestral tribe according to the number of names on the list.
26.56: Each grant of land must be assigned by lot among the larger and smaller tribal groups.”
26.57: This is the record of the Levites who were counted according to their clans: The Gershonite clan, named after their ancestor Gershon. The Kohathite clan, named after their ancestor Kohath. The Merarite clan, named after their ancestor Merari.
26.58: The Libnites, the Hebronites, the Mahlites, the Mushites, and the Korahites were all subclans of the Levites. Now Kohath was the ancestor of Amram,
26.59: and Amram’s wife was named Jochebed. She also was a descendant of Levi, born among the Levites in the land of Egypt. Amram and Jochebed became the parents of Aaron, Moses, and their sister, Miriam.
26.60: To Aaron were born Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
26.61: But Nadab and Abihu died when they burned before the Lord the wrong kind of fire, different than he had commanded.
26.62: The men from the Levite clans who were one month old or older numbered 23,000. But the Levites were not included in the registration of the rest of the people of Israel because they were not given an allotment of land when it was divided among the Israelites.
26.63: So these are the results of the registration of the people of Israel as conducted by Moses and Eleazar the priest on the plains of Moab beside the Jordan River, across from Jericho.
26.64: Not one person on this list had been among those listed in the previous registration taken by Moses and Aaron in the wilderness of Sinai.
26.65: For the Lord had said of them, “They will all die in the wilderness.” Not one of them survived except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

30.1: Then Moses summoned the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “This is what the Lord has commanded:
30.2: A man who makes a vow to the Lord or makes a pledge under oath must never break it. He must do exactly what he said he would do.
30.3: “If a young woman makes a vow to the Lord or a pledge under oath while she is still living at her father’s home,
30.4: and her father hears of the vow or pledge and does not object to it, then all her vows and pledges will stand.
30.5: But if her father refuses to let her fulfill the vow or pledge on the day he hears of it, then all her vows and pledges will become invalid. The Lord will forgive her because her father would not let her fulfill them.
30.6: “Now suppose a young woman makes a vow or binds herself with an impulsive pledge and later marries.
30.7: If her husband learns of her vow or pledge and does not object on the day he hears of it, her vows and pledges will stand.
30.8: But if her husband refuses to accept her vow or impulsive pledge on the day he hears of it, he nullifies her commitments, and the Lord will forgive her.
30.9: If, however, a woman is a widow or is divorced, she must fulfill all her vows and pledges.
30.10: “But suppose a woman is married and living in her husband’s home when she makes a vow or binds herself with a pledge.
30.11: If her husband hears of it and does not object to it, her vow or pledge will stand.
30.12: But if her husband refuses to accept it on the day he hears of it, her vow or pledge will be nullified, and the Lord will forgive her.
30.13: So her husband may either confirm or nullify any vows or pledges she makes to deny herself.
30.14: But if he does not object on the day he hears of it, then he is agreeing to all her vows and pledges.
30.15: If he waits more than a day and then tries to nullify a vow or pledge, he will be punished for her guilt.”
30.16: These are the regulations the Lord gave Moses concerning relationships between a man and his wife, and between a father and a young daughter who still lives at home.

10.1: Now the Lord said to Moses,
10.2: “Make two trumpets of hammered silver for calling the community to assemble and for signaling the breaking of camp.
10.3: When both trumpets are blown, everyone must gather before you at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
10.4: But if only one trumpet is blown, then only the leaders—the heads of the clans of Israel—must present themselves to you.
10.5: “When you sound the signal to move on, the tribes camped on the east side of the Tabernacle must break camp and move forward.
10.6: When you sound the signal a second time, the tribes camped on the south will follow. You must sound short blasts as the signal for moving on.
10.7: But when you call the people to an assembly, blow the trumpets with a different signal.
10.8: Only the priests, Aaron’s descendants, are allowed to blow the trumpets. This is a permanent law for you, to be observed from generation to generation.
10.9: “When you arrive in your own land and go to war against your enemies who attack you, sound the alarm with the trumpets. Then the Lord your God will remember you and rescue you from your enemies.
10.10: Blow the trumpets in times of gladness, too, sounding them at your annual festivals and at the beginning of each month. And blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and peace offerings. The trumpets will remind your God of his covenant with you. I am the Lord your God.”
10.11: In the second year after Israel’s departure from Egypt—on the twentieth day of the second month—the cloud lifted from the Tabernacle of the Covenant.
10.12: So the Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sinai and traveled on from place to place until the cloud stopped in the wilderness of Paran.
10.13: When the people set out for the first time, following the instructions the Lord had given through Moses,
10.14: Judah’s troops led the way. They marched behind their banner, and their leader was Nahshon son of Amminadab.
10.15: They were joined by the troops of the tribe of Issachar, led by Nethanel son of Zuar,
10.16: and the troops of the tribe of Zebulun, led by Eliab son of Helon.
10.17: Then the Tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonite and Merarite divisions of the Levites were next in the line of march, carrying the Tabernacle with them.
10.18: Reuben’s troops went next, marching behind their banner. Their leader was Elizur son of Shedeur.
10.19: They were joined by the troops of the tribe of Simeon, led by Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai,
10.20: and the troops of the tribe of Gad, led by Eliasaph son of Deuel.
10.21: Next came the Kohathite division of the Levites, carrying the sacred objects from the Tabernacle. Before they arrived at the next camp, the Tabernacle would already be set up at its new location.
10.22: Ephraim’s troops went next, marching behind their banner. Their leader was Elishama son of Ammihud.
10.23: They were joined by the troops of the tribe of Manasseh, led by Gamaliel son of Pedahzur,
10.24: and the troops of the tribe of Benjamin, led by Abidan son of Gideoni.
10.25: Dan’s troops went last, marching behind their banner and serving as the rear guard for all the tribal camps. Their leader was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
10.26: They were joined by the troops of the tribe of Asher, led by Pagiel son of Ocran,
10.27: and the troops of the tribe of Naphtali, led by Ahira son of Enan.
10.28: This was the order in which the Israelites marched, division by division.
10.29: One day Moses said to his brother-in-law, Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, “We are on our way to the place the Lord promised us, for he said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us and we will treat you well, for the Lord has promised wonderful blessings for Israel!”
10.30: But Hobab replied, “No, I will not go. I must return to my own land and family.”
10.31: “Please don’t leave us,” Moses pleaded. “You know the places in the wilderness where we should camp. Come, be our guide.
10.32: If you do, we’ll share with you all the blessings the Lord gives us.”
10.33: They marched for three days after leaving the mountain of the Lord, with the Ark of the Lord’s Covenant moving ahead of them to show them where to stop and rest.
10.34: As they moved on each day, the cloud of the Lord hovered over them.
10.35: And whenever the Ark set out, Moses would shout, “Arise, O Lord, and let your enemies be scattered! Let them flee before you!”
10.36: And when the Ark was set down, he would say, “Return, O Lord, to the countless thousands of Israel!”

21.1: The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that the Israelites were approaching on the road through Atharim. So he attacked the Israelites and took some of them as prisoners.
21.2: Then the people of Israel made this vow to the Lord: “If you will hand these people over to us, we will completely destroy all their towns.”
21.3: The Lord heard the Israelites’ request and gave them victory over the Canaanites. The Israelites completely destroyed them and their towns, and the place has been called Hormah ever since.
21.4: Then the people of Israel set out from Mount Hor, taking the road to the Red Sea to go around the land of Edom. But the people grew impatient with the long journey,
21.5: and they began to speak against God and Moses. “Why have you brought us out of Egypt to die here in the wilderness?” they complained. “There is nothing to eat here and nothing to drink. And we hate this horrible manna!”
21.6: So the Lord sent poisonous snakes among the people, and many were bitten and died.
21.7: Then the people came to Moses and cried out, “We have sinned by speaking against the Lord and against you. Pray that the Lord will take away the snakes.” So Moses prayed for the people.
21.8: Then the Lord told him, “Make a replica of a poisonous snake and attach it to a pole. All who are bitten will live if they simply look at it!”
21.9: So Moses made a snake out of bronze and attached it to a pole. Then anyone who was bitten by a snake could look at the bronze snake and be healed!
21.10: The Israelites traveled next to Oboth and camped there.
21.11: Then they went on to Iye-abarim, in the wilderness on the eastern border of Moab.
21.12: From there they traveled to the valley of Zered Brook and set up camp.
21.13: Then they moved out and camped on the far side of the Arnon River, in the wilderness adjacent to the territory of the Amorites. The Arnon is the boundary line between the Moabites and the Amorites.
21.14: For this reason The Book of the Wars of the Lord speaks of “the town of Waheb in the area of Suphah, and the ravines of the Arnon River,
21.15: and the ravines that extend as far as the settlement of Ar on the border of Moab.”
21.16: From there the Israelites traveled to Beer, which is the well where the Lord said to Moses, “Assemble the people, and I will give them water.”
21.17: There the Israelites sang this song: “Spring up, O well! Yes, sing its praises!
21.18: Sing of this well, which princes dug, which great leaders hollowed out with their scepters and staffs.” Then the Israelites left the wilderness and proceeded on through Mattanah,
21.20: After that they went to the valley in Moab where Pisgah Peak overlooks the wasteland.
21.21: The Israelites sent ambassadors to King Sihon of the Amorites with this message:
21.22: “Let us travel through your land. We will be careful not to go through your fields and vineyards. We won’t even drink water from your wells. We will stay on the king’s road until we have passed through your territory.”
21.23: But King Sihon refused to let them cross his territory. Instead, he mobilized his entire army and attacked Israel in the wilderness, engaging them in battle at Jahaz.
21.24: But the Israelites slaughtered them with their swords and occupied their land from the Arnon River to the Jabbok River. They went only as far as the Ammonite border because the boundary of the Ammonites was fortified.
21.25: So Israel captured all the towns of the Amorites and settled in them, including the city of Heshbon and its surrounding villages.
21.26: Heshbon had been the capital of King Sihon of the Amorites. He had defeated a former Moabite king and seized all his land as far as the Arnon River.
21.27: Therefore, the ancient poets wrote this about him: “Come to Heshbon and let it be rebuilt! Let the city of Sihon be restored.
21.28: A fire flamed forth from Heshbon, a blaze from the city of Sihon. It burned the city of Ar in Moab; it destroyed the rulers of the Arnon heights.
21.29: What sorrow awaits you, O people of Moab! You are finished, O worshipers of Chemosh! Chemosh has left his sons as refugees, his daughters as captives of Sihon, the Amorite king.
21.30: We have utterly destroyed them, from Heshbon to Dibon. We have completely wiped them out as far away as Nophah and Medeba.”
21.31: So the people of Israel occupied the territory of the Amorites.
21.32: After Moses sent men to explore the Jazer area, they captured all the towns in the region and drove out the Amorites who lived there.
21.33: Then they turned and marched up the road to Bashan, but King Og of Bashan and all his people attacked them at Edrei.
21.34: The Lord said to Moses, “Do not be afraid of him, for I have handed him over to you, along with all his people and his land. Do the same to him as you did to King Sihon of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon.”
21.35: And Israel killed King Og, his sons, and all his subjects; not a single survivor remained. Then Israel occupied their land.

17.1: Then the Lord said to Moses,
17.2: “Tell the people of Israel to bring you twelve wooden staffs, one from each leader of Israel’s ancestral tribes, and inscribe each leader’s name on his staff.
17.3: Inscribe Aaron’s name on the staff of the tribe of Levi, for there must be one staff for the leader of each ancestral tribe.
17.4: Place these staffs in the Tabernacle in front of the Ark containing the tablets of the Covenant, where I meet with you.
17.5: Buds will sprout on the staff belonging to the man I choose. Then I will finally put an end to the people’s murmuring and complaining against you.”
17.6: So Moses gave the instructions to the people of Israel, and each of the twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron, brought Moses a staff.
17.7: Moses placed the staffs in the Lord’s presence in the Tabernacle of the Covenant.
17.8: When he went into the Tabernacle of the Covenant the next day, he found that Aaron’s staff, representing the tribe of Levi, had sprouted, budded, blossomed, and produced ripe almonds!
17.9: When Moses brought all the staffs out from the Lord’s presence, he showed them to the people. Each man claimed his own staff.
17.10: And the Lord said to Moses: “Place Aaron’s staff permanently before the Ark of the Covenant to serve as a warning to rebels. This should put an end to their complaints against me and prevent any further deaths.”
17.11: So Moses did as the Lord commanded him.
17.12: Then the people of Israel said to Moses, “Look, we are doomed! We are dead! We are ruined!
17.13: Everyone who even comes close to the Tabernacle of the Lord dies. Are we all doomed to die?”

7.1: On the day Moses set up the Tabernacle, he anointed it and set it apart as holy. He also anointed and set apart all its furnishings and the altar with its utensils.
7.2: Then the leaders of Israel—the tribal leaders who had registered the troops—came and brought their offerings.
7.3: Together they brought six large wagons and twelve oxen. There was a wagon for every two leaders and an ox for each leader. They presented these to the Lord in front of the Tabernacle.
7.4: Then the Lord said to Moses,
7.5: “Receive their gifts, and use these oxen and wagons for transporting the Tabernacle. Distribute them among the Levites according to the work they have to do.”
7.6: So Moses took the wagons and oxen and presented them to the Levites.
7.7: He gave two wagons and four oxen to the Gershonite division for their work,
